Watts made this hymn from Psalm 127, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor in vain; unless the LORD protects the city, its watchmen stand guard in vain. 2In vain you rise early and stay up late, toiling for bread to eat— for He gives sleep to His beloved. 3Children are indeed a heritage from the LORD, and the fruit of the womb is His reward. 4Like arrows in the hand of a warrior, so are children born in one’s youth. … 1 more verses PSALM 127 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 127
If God succeed not, all the cost And pains to build the house are lost: If God the city will not keep, The watchful guards as well may sleep. STANZA I
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 1. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
